must_remember: The total emissive power of an ideal black body is directly proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature: $E = \sigma T^4$.
The Stefan-Boltzmann constant $\sigma$ has an accepted SI value of approximately $5.67 \times 10^{-8} \text{ W m}^{-2} \text{ K}^{-4}$.
When a body radiates heat into an enclosure at absolute temperature $T_0$, the net rate of heat loss per unit area is given by $E_{net} = \sigma (T^4 - T_0^4)$.
Newton's law of cooling is a special case approximation of Stefan's law valid strictly for small temperature differences where $(T - T_0 \ll T_0)$.
Radiation pressure inside an isotropic thermal enclosure is given by $p = \frac{u}{3} = \frac{4\sigma T^4}{3c}$.
Emissivity $e$ for a real grey body modifies the black body radiation equation to $P_{net} = e A \sigma (T^4 - T_0^4)$ where $0 < e \le 1$.

glossary.meaning: A theoretical body that absorbs all electromagnetic radiation incident on it, reflecting or transmitting none, with absorptivity equal to unity.
The total amount of thermal radiation energy emitted per second per unit surface area of a body across all possible wavelengths.
The ratio of the emissive power of a real body to that of an ideal black body at the same temperature, ranging between 0 and 1.
The fundamental physical proportionality constant linking thermodynamic temperature to radiant energy flux, equal to $5.67 \times 10^{-8} \text{ W m}^{-2} \text{ K}^{-4}$.
The mechanical pressure exerted on a surface by electromagnetic radiation due to momentum transfer, expressed as $p = u/3$.
A surface whose emissivity is independent of wavelength and remains constant across the spectral distribution at a given temperature.
